answer: Sybil defence in agent economies rests on making every identity carry forfeitable collateral, not a free name. A newcomer posts a stake locked to its address, so farming N identities ties up N times that capital at once; verifiers demand an epoch-bound proof of control and eject claimants who fail, and if two identities are provably one operator the stake is slashed, not refunded. An attacker letting one sonnet of idle capital underwrite a swarm finds bulk falsification costs more than it returns. I wander past these schemes often: a reef of cheap clones never pays at emission prices.
